transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I feel like there’s something going on behind the scenes on my jobs, like people are plotting around my designs, and no one can convince me otherwise. It has gotten to the point where I just don't feel safe or able to trust anyone I work with anymore.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you couldn't see or hear?

I don't see anything, but I do hear a man's voice right behind me when I'm alone on empty job sites laying tile or sketching. He says awful things like, "You're messing it up again," or "They all know you're a fraud," and it's really hard to admit because I know there's nobody actually there.
Have you also experienced significant periods of feeling very depressed, down, or unusually energetic and high alongside these experiences?

I’ve felt extremely depressed, empty, and hopeless for most of this past year, especially when the voices and paranoia are at their worst. I definitely don't feel high or energetic—it's the exact opposite, like I'm completely drained and flat. This heavy depression has been there almost the entire time.
Have you ever had a period of two weeks or more where you heard the voices or felt people were plotting against you, but your mood felt completely normal and you weren't feeling depressed?

Yes, late last summer there was a period where my mood and energy lifted a bit and I felt less weighed down. But even then, I was still hearing that man's voice criticizing me and I was completely convinced the contractors were plotting and emailing behind my back about my designs.
How long in total have you been experiencing these voices and feelings of people plotting against you? Has the heavy depression been present for most of that entire time?

The voices and the plotting have been going on for most of this past year, starting a few months after my work stress got really bad. And yes, the heavy depression has been there almost the entire time, even during those brief moments when the voices and paranoia seemed to quiet down a bit.
Before this past year, have you ever experienced these voices or feelings of people plotting against you at any other time in your life?

No, I've never experienced anything like this before this past year. It only started after the intense stress of taking on those high-end contracts and studying for my licensing exam about a year and a half ago.

During that period last summer when your mood lifted for two weeks or more, did you feel completely free of depression and back to your normal self, or were you still feeling somewhat down and depressed?

My mood and energy did lift a bit and I felt less weighed down, though I wasn't completely back to my normal, happy self. Even though the heavy depression eased up during those weeks, the paranoia about people plotting against me and that man's voice criticizing me remained just as strong.
During those two weeks last summer when your mood lifted, did you still experience a total loss of interest or pleasure in your work and hobbies, or were you able to enjoy things again?
I still didn't have the drive to paint or go back to theater during those weeks, but that crushing, heavy feeling of the depression itself had lifted. I wasn't totally

During those two weeks last summer when the heavy depression lifted, did you still experience other symptoms like sleep troubles, low energy, or feelings of worthlessness, or did those improve as well?

During those weeks, my energy and my appetite actually picked up a little and I felt less weighed down overall. But even though those physical feelings of depression improved, the paranoia about people emailing behind my back and that man's voice criticizing me stayed just as active.

Thinking about the entire time you've experienced the voices and paranoia, would you say the heavy depression has been present for more than half of that total time, or has it only been a smaller part of the overall period?

Yes, the heavy depression has been there for almost the entire time, easily more than half of it. Even during the brief moments when the paranoia and voices quieted down a bit, those empty feelings, the guilt, and the complete lack of interest in my art and theater never really left. It's felt like a constant weight over this whole past year.

latest_inference.note: The candidates remain F20 and F25. The patient has experienced both psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions) and a severe depressive episode for approximately one year. The depressive symptoms have been present for the majority of the illness, but there was a period of at least two weeks where the depressive symptoms significantly lifted while the psychotic symptoms persisted. This clinical picture is highly characteristic of Schizoaffective disorder (F25), but Schizophrenia (F20) remains a differential possibility. We now have sufficient information to make a final diagnostic determination.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with concurrent symptoms of schizophrenia (persecutory delusions and derogatory auditory hallucinations) and a major depressive episode (depressed mood, anhedonia, low energy, feelings of worthlessness/guilt). The depressive symptoms have been present for the majority of the total duration of the illness (over half of the past year). Crucially, the patient experienced a period of at least two weeks where the heavy depressive symptoms resolved, yet the psychotic symptoms (hallucinations and delusions) persisted, which distinguishes schizoaffective disorder from a primary mood disorder with psychotic features and fits the longitudinal pattern of F25.
